verses.zh: 所罗门建造耶和华殿和王宫，二十年才完毕了。
verses.en: After twenty years, during which Solomon built the Lord’s temple and his royal palace,
verses.commentary:
8:1 The parallel is in 1 Kgs. 9:10-28. Josephus, Antiq. 8.5.1., explains "the twenty years" as seven for the
temple and thirteen for the palace. He describes the palace in 1 Chr. 8.5.2.

verses.zh: 以后所罗门重新修筑希兰送给他的那些城邑，使以色列人住在那里。
verses.en: Solomon rebuilt the cities that Huram[NOTE:1] had given him and settled Israelites there.
notes: Heb “Huram” (also in v. 18). Some medieval Hebrew mss, along with the LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate spell the name “Hiram,” agreeing with 1 Chr 14:1. “Huram” is a variant spelling referring to the same individual.
verses.commentary:
8:2 "Huram" In 2 Sam. 5:1; 1 Chr. 14:1 he is named "Hiram, King of Tyre."

"the cities which Huram had given to him" In the parallel of 1 Kgs. 9:10-14, it is Solomon who gave Huram the cities.
We learn from 1 Kgs. 9:11 that Hiram did not like the cities Solomon gave him and may have returned them. The gold mentioned
in 2 Chr. 8:17-18 may have gone to Hiram as a payment.

verses.zh: 所罗门往哈马琐巴去，攻取了那地方。
verses.en: Solomon went to Hamath Zobah and seized it.
verses.commentary: 8:3 This military campaign is not recorded in Kings.

verses.zh: 所罗门建造旷野里的达莫，又建造哈马所有的积货城，
verses.en: He built up Tadmor in the wilderness and all the storage cities he had built in Hamath.
verses.commentary:
8:4 "Tadmor" The 1 Kgs. 9:18 verse has "Tamar." In a context extolling Solomon's building projects and military
conquests, the small village of Tamar seems inappropriate. Tadmor was a major city 125 miles NE of Damascus on a major
trade route (later called Palmyra). Modern commentators surmised Solomon fortified this city as a message to Mesopotamian
empires!

Solomon took full advantage of the weakness of the empires of Egypt and Mesopotamia to expand and fortify
his empire.

verses.zh: 又建造上伯・和仑、下伯・和仑作为保障，都有墙，有门，有闩；
verses.en: He made upper Beth Horon and lower Beth Horon fortified cities with walls and barred gates,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and he built…[as] cities of fortification, [with] walls, doors, and a bar.”
verses.commentary:
8:5 The two cities mentioned in 2 Chr. 8:5 controlled a pass between Jerusalem and Joppa. It was part of the larger
fortification of Jerusalem.

verses.zh: 又建造巴拉和所有的积货城，并屯车辆马兵的城，与耶路撒冷、黎巴嫩，以及自己治理的全国中所愿意建造的。
verses.en: and built up Baalath, all the storage cities that belonged to him,[NOTE:1] and all the cities where chariots and horses were kept.[NOTE:2] He built whatever he wanted in Jerusalem,[NOTE:3] Lebanon, and throughout his entire kingdom.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “Solomon.” The recurrence of the proper name is unexpected in terms of contemporary English style, so the pronoun has been used in the translation instead.
Heb “the cities of the chariots and the cities of the horses.”
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “and all the desire of Solomon which he desired to build in Jerusalem and in Lebanon and in all the land of his kingdom.”

verses.zh: 至于国中所剩下不属以色列人的赫人、亚摩利人、比利洗人、希未人、耶布斯人，
verses.en: Now several non-Israelite peoples were left in the land after the conquest of Joshua, including the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “all the people who were left from the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, who were not from Israel.”
verses.commentary:
8:7 See
SPECIAL TOPIC: PRE-ISRAELITE INHABITANTS OF PALESTINE.

verses.zh: 就是以色列人未曾灭绝的，所罗门挑取他们的后裔作服苦的奴仆，直到今日。
verses.en: Their descendants remained in the land (the Israelites were unable to wipe them out). Solomon conscripted them for his work crews, and they continue in that role to this very day.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “from their sons who were left after them in the land, whom the sons of Israel did not wipe out, and Solomon raised them up for a work crew to this day.”
verses.commentary:
8:8 "Solomon raised as forced laborers" The commander of this group is mentioned in 1 Kgs. 4:6. This practice was
common in the ANE.

"to this day" See note at 2 Chr. 5:9.

verses.zh: 惟有以色列人，所罗门不使他们当奴仆做工，乃是作他的战士、军长的统领、车兵长、马兵长。
verses.en: Solomon did not assign Israelites to these work crews;[NOTE:1] the Israelites served as his soldiers, officers, charioteers, and commanders of his chariot forces.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and from the sons of Israel whom Solomon did not assign to the laborers for his work.”
Heb “officers of his chariots and his horses.”

verses.zh: 所罗门王有二百五十督工的，监管工人。
verses.en: These men worked for King Solomon as supervisors; there were a total of 250 of them who were in charge of the people.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “these [were] the officials of the governors who belonged to the king, Solomon, 250, the ones ruling over the people.”

verses.zh: 所罗门将法老的女儿带出大卫城，上到为她建造的宫里；因所罗门说：「耶和华约柜所到之处都为圣地，所以我的妻不可住在以色列王大卫的宫里。」
verses.en: Solomon moved Pharaoh’s daughter up from the City of David[NOTE:1] to the palace he had built for her, for he said, “My wife must not live in the palace of King David of Israel, for the places where the ark of the Lord has entered are holy.”
notes: The phrase the City of David refers here to the fortress of Zion in Jerusalem, not to Bethlehem. See 2 Sam 5:7.
verses.commentary:
8:11 The parallel in 1 Kgs. 9:23 has 550 supervisors, while this text has 250. No one knows why the numbers in
Samuel ‒ Kings do not agree with Chronicles. Here are the theories.

- a scribal error

- the numbers are used symbolically to show Solomon's greatness

- there were different Hebrew texts behind each one

- they represent different oral traditions (see John H. Walton and D. Brent Sandy, The Lost World of Scripture)

The best study so far on this subject is Edwin Thiele, The Mysterious Numbers of the Hebrew Kings.
If the numbers relate to years of a king's reign, then possibly

- use of two calendars

- use of two ways to count the ascension year

- the problem of co-reigns

This verse shows Solomon's respect for the city of David. He moves his foreign wife to a special palace he
built for her.

The Chronicler omits all the terrible things Solomon did with his foreign wives in his old age (cf. 1 Kings 11).

In this chapter Solomon is depicted as

- following the commands of David faithfully

- being victorious in battle

- building many projects throughout his domain

- starting a fleet of ships to bring gold

verses.zh: 所罗门在耶和华的坛上，就是在廊子前他所筑的坛上，与耶和华献燔祭；
verses.en: Then Solomon offered burnt sacrifices to the Lord on the altar of the Lord which he had built in front of the temple’s porch.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the porch.”
verses.commentary:
8:12 This is surprising, since Uzziah was condemned for offering a sacrifice; that was a priest's duty.

Earlier at the dedication of the temple, Solomon "blessed" the people (cf. 2 Chr. 6:3), which was also an
act reserved for priests.

verses.zh: 又遵着摩西的吩咐在安息日、月朔，并一年三节，就是除酵节、七七节、住棚节，献每日所当献的祭。
verses.en: He observed the daily requirements for sacrifices that Moses had specified for Sabbaths, new moon festivals, and the three annual celebrations—the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Shelters.[NOTE:1]
notes: The Hebrew phrase הַסֻּכּוֹת[חַג] (khag hassukkot, “[Feast of] shelters” [or “huts”]) is traditionally known as the Feast of Tabernacles. The rendering “booths” (cf. NAB, NASB, NRSV) is probably better than the traditional “tabernacles” in light of the meaning of the term סֻכָּה (sukkah, “hut; booth”), but “booths” are frequently associated with trade shows and craft fairs in contemporary American English. The nature of the celebration during this feast as a commemoration of the wanderings of the Israelites after they left Egypt suggests that a translation like “shelters” is more appropriate.
verses.commentary:
8:13 "sabbaths" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: SABBATH (OT).

"the new moons" Many commentators assume that this festival gained popularity after the exile because it is mentioned
often in 1 and 2 Chronicles.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOON WORSHIP

"the annual feasts" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FEASTS OF ISRAEL.

verses.zh: 所罗门照着他父大卫所定的例，派定祭司的班次，使他们各供己事，又使利未人各尽其职，赞美耶和华，在祭司面前做每日所当做的；又派守门的按着班次看守各门，因为神人大卫是这样吩咐的。
verses.en: As his father David had decreed, Solomon[NOTE:1] appointed the divisions of the priests to do their assigned tasks, the Levitical orders to lead worship and help the priests with their daily tasks,[NOTE:2] and the divisions of the gatekeepers to serve at their assigned gates.[NOTE:3] This was what David the man of God had ordered.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Solomon) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “and the Levites, according to their posts, to praise and to serve opposite the priests according to the matter of a day in its day.”
Heb “and the gatekeepers by their divisions for a gate and a gate.”
Heb “for so [was] the command of David the man of God.”
verses.commentary:
8:14 Solomon was faithful to the commands of David his father.

- The division of priests is found in 1 Chronicles 24.

- The divisions of Levites in 1 Chronicles 15.

- The divisions of "gatekeepers" is found in 1 Chronicles 26.

"David the man of God" David is called by this title in Neh. 12:24,36. Moses was the first to be called by this title
(cf. Deut. 33:1; Josh. 14:6). Later, other prophets bore this honorific designation. See NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 390, #9.

verses.zh: 王所吩咐众祭司和利未人的，无论是管府库或办别的事，他们都不违背。
verses.en: They did not neglect any detail of the king’s orders pertaining to the priests, Levites, and treasuries.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and they did not turn aside from the command of the king concerning the priests and the Levites with regard to any matter and with regard to the treasuries.”

verses.zh: 所罗门建造耶和华的殿，从立根基直到成功的日子，工料俱备。这样，耶和华的殿全然完毕。
verses.en: All the work ordered by Solomon was completed, from the day the foundation of the Lord’s temple was laid until it was finished; the Lord’s temple was completed.

verses.zh: 那时，所罗门往以东地靠海的以旬・迦别和以禄去。
verses.en: Then Solomon went to Ezion Geber and to Elat on the coast in the land of Edom.
verses.commentary:
8:17 "Ezion-geber" This was the major city at the north end of the Gulf of Aqaba. It was the major southern seaport
for Solomon's trading endeavors.

verses.zh: 希兰差遣他的臣仆，将船只和熟悉泛海的仆人送到所罗门那里。他们同着所罗门的仆人到了俄斐，得了四百五十他连得金子，运到所罗门王那里。
verses.en: Huram sent him ships and some of his sailors, men who were well acquainted with the sea. They sailed with Solomon’s men to Ophir[NOTE:1] and took from there 450 talents[NOTE:2] of gold, which they brought back to King Solomon.
notes: Heb “and Huram sent to him by the hand of his servants, ships, and servants [who] know the sea, and they came with the servants of Solomon to Ophir.”

The Hebrew word כִּכַּר (kikkar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or, by extension, to a standard unit of weight. According to the older (Babylonian) standard the “talent” weighed 130 lbs. (58.9 kg), but later this was lowered to 108.3 lbs. (49.1 kg). More recent research suggests the “light” standard talent was 67.3 lbs. (30.6 kg). Using this as the standard for calculation, the weight of the gold was 30,285 lbs. (13,770 kg).
verses.commentary:
8:18 Solomon's fleet was made up of Phoenician ships and sailors (cf. 1 Kgs. 9:26-28).

"Ophir" See note at 1 Chr. 29:4. It was the source or marketplace for (cf. 1 Kgs. 9:28; 10:11):

- expensive woods

- jewels

- gold

See Edwin Yamauchi, The Stones and the Scriptures, pp. 69071; NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 321-322.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why are the events different between Samuel/Kings and Chronicles?

- Did Solomon give Huram 20 cities or vice versa?

- Why are the numbers different between Samuel/Kings and Chronicles?

- Who did Solomon use to build his projects?

- Why did Solomon move Pharaoh's daughter out of the "city of David"?

- Does Solomon perform priestly duties in 2 Chr. 8:12? (cf. 2 Chr. 6:4)

- Why are "the commandments" of both Moses (2 Chr. 8:13) and David (2 Chr. 8:14) mentioned?

- Why is the large amount of gold mentioned in 2 Chr. 8:18?
